draft.title: Parametric equations
card: In parametric equations, x and y are each given in terms of a third variable t, called the parameter. Each value of t gives one point (x, y).
To find a point, put the value of t into both equations. For x = t² + 1 and y = 3t, t = 1 gives the point (2, 3).
To find the Cartesian equation, make t the subject of one equation and substitute it into the other. For x = 2t and y = t + 1, t = x/2, so y = x/2 + 1.
Parametric equations can trace curves that are not graphs of a single function. The equations x = r cos t and y = r sin t trace a circle x² + y² = r² as t increases.
draft.remember: Put t into both equations for a point. Eliminate t for the Cartesian equation.

a.q: A curve has x = t² + 1 and y = 3t. What point is on the curve when t = 2?
a.why: When t = 2, x = 2² + 1 = 5 and y = 3 × 2 = 6, so the point is (5, 6). The point (4, 6) leaves out the + 1. The point (6, 5) swaps x and y.
a.clue: Put t = 2 into each equation separately.

b.q: A curve has x = t + 2 and y = t². What is its Cartesian equation?
b.why: From x = t + 2, t = x − 2. Substituting into y = t² gives y = (x − 2)². The option y = x² − 2 squares x instead of squaring the whole expression for t.
b.clue: Make t the subject first, then square it.
